fullPassage:
History, people often say, repeats itself. And looking at the historical records of the ancient civilizations, some things do seem to happen again and again.

(A) If so, archaeology would be pretty boring: one thing would happen again and again. But that's not what archaeologists see. Some civilizations end suddenly, like the Aztec and Inca, conquered by invaders in the 1520s AD.

(B) Civilizations expand, get overextended, and then collapse as in the cases of Rome, which went under in 476 AD, and the British Empire, which fell apart more than a thousand years later in the post-World War II era. But is this always the case?

(C) Those empires never had the chance to collapse as a result of overexpansion. So in the case of civilizations, "history repeats itself" seems to be an oversimplification.

If so, archaeology would be pretty boring: one thing would happen again and again. But that's not ③<u>that</u> archaeologists see. Some civilizations end suddenly, like the Aztec and Inca, ④<u>conquered</u> by invaders in the 1520s AD.

det.korean: ③ that → what: 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what이 필요 (see의 목적어 역할)
det.analysis:
✅ ① repeats: 주어 History(3인칭 단수) — 적절
✅ ② seem: 주어 some things(복수) + do 뒤 원형 — 적절
❌ ③ that → what: '고고학자들이 보는 것'이므로 선행사 포함 관계대명사 what
✅ ④ conquered: 과거분사(수동) — 적절
det.tip: what = the thing(s) that — 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사

questions.passage: History, people often say, repeats itself. And looking at the historical records of the ancient civilizations, some things do seem to happen again and again. But that's not what archaeologists see. Some civilizations end suddenly, conquered by invaders. Others expand, get overextended, and collapse. questions.stem: 윗글의 요약문으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 모든 문명은 팽창과 붕괴의 동일한 순환을 겪는다.
침략에 의한 멸망이 과잉 팽창보다 더 흔하다.
문명의 흥망 패턴은 다양하므로 '역사 반복'은 지나친 단순화이다.

det.korean: 글의 핵심: 문명의 흥망 패턴은 다양 → 역사 반복 = 단순화
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 정확한 요약
❌ ① 동일한 순환 — 글의 요지와 반대
❌ ② 고고학이 반복을 증명 — 반대
❌ ④ 비교 빈도 — 언급 없음
det.tip: 요약 = 핵심 주장의 축약

questions.passage:
History, people often say, repeats itself. And looking at the historical records of the ancient civilizations, some things do seem to happen again and again.

(A) If so, archaeology would be pretty boring: one thing would happen again and again. But that's not what archaeologists see. Some civilizations end suddenly, like the Aztec and Inca, conquered by invaders in the 1520s AD.

(B) Civilizations expand, get overextended, and then collapse as in the cases of Rome, which went under in 476 AD, and the British Empire, which fell apart more than a thousand years later in the post-World War II era. But is this always the case?

(C) ____ So in the case of civilizations, "history repeats itself" seems to be an oversimplification.
